# 3-D shear-decay ladder: closing the missing resolutions

**Artifact**: `benchmarks/threed_shear/report.json` (regenerated by `run.py --merge`), per-case JSON under `benchmarks/threed_shear/cases/`; figure `benchmarks/threed_shear/figures/threed_shear.png`.

This document is generated by `scripts/make_doc_threed_shear_ladder.py`; every number below is read from the artifact.

## 1. Case and reference

Case: 3-D double-shear (unsteady Stokes) on a triply periodic cube.

Reference: u = A sin(ky) sin(kz) exp(-2 nu k^2 t); decay rate 2 nu k^2.

| parameter | value |
|---|---|
| `box` | 1.0 |
| `nu` | 0.05 |
| `amplitude` | 0.1 |
| `sound_speed` | 10.0 |
| `periods` | 1 |
| `h_over_dx_default` | 1.3 |
| `fourth_order_coefficient` | beta_i = I4_i/120, I4_i = sum_j V_j r^4 lap_i W_ij (kernel-lattice moment, continuum value 18 h^2) |

## 2. Method

A velocity field `u = A sin(ky) sin(kz)` on a triply periodic cube decays as `exp(-2 nu k^2 t)` for the Stokes (creeping) limit. The SPH momentum equation is advanced with the Tait equation of state; the fitted decay rate of the discrete kinetic energy is compared with `2 nu k^2`. The viscous operator is the renormalised Laplacian (Trask et al. 2015 form) and, for the fourth-order rungs, the two-pass operator of `benchmarks/threed_shear/fourth_order.py`.

## 5. Notes, limitations

1. The `mu = 0` control is not part of this ladder; the spurious-dissipation floor of the scheme is measured separately in the 2-D Taylor-Green case (`docs/benchmarks/taylor-green.md`).
2. `kh` is reported per rung because the decay-rate error of a particle viscous operator is a function of `kh`, not of `n` alone; at `kh` well below 1 the truncation error is small and at `kh` approaching 1 it is not.
3. The ladder is a verification of the viscous operator against an exact Stokes solution, not a validation against measurement.
